statement: Where a capability's circuit is resolved from when it is not packaged beside the workbench. The estate's compiled topology is a product of the platform; 218 capabilities of it are far larger than a workbench package, so the package carries the catalogue and resolves scene bytes on demand.

resolver.note: The response carries the lowered circuit-scene.v1 document and its screened artifact together, so a scene and the bytes it describes cannot be fetched out of step with one another.

rationale: the browser receives a resolved scene rather than a compiled product it would have to interpret
screening that rejects scripts, inline handlers and unapproved references runs before any bytes reach a page
a refused scene is refused once, at the boundary, rather than by every consumer

divergent.materials[].retained: the local adapter copies textures; the server references the ones the platform already serves
divergent.scene.retained: null on the server; the artifact is resolved from its source rather than copied
divergent.scene.source: server only; names the product the scene was lowered from
divergent.provenance.adapter.name: lower-scene, because a different adapter produced it
divergent.provenance.ingestedFrom.path: served-relative on the server, which does not disclose host filesystem paths

governance.note: Resolving a circuit reads a compiled product. It is not registered estate authority and confers no admission.

refusalCodes.SCENE_IDENTITY_INVALID: The capability or view identity is not the shape the compiler emits.
refusalCodes.VIEW_IDENTITY_MISMATCH: The product found at that path declares a different view.
refusalCodes.SCENE_REFUSED: The scene did not pass screening, so neither its graph nor its bytes are served.
refusalCodes.SCENE_UNAVAILABLE: No compiled view exists at that identity.
